MoreSpace/Industries/Real estate/Residential developers

Turn portal enquiries into site visits, bookings and on-time collections

Developers juggle launches, inventory, channel partners, banks and buyers at different stages, all at once. We connect portals, WhatsApp, the CRM and the ERP so leads are answered fast, visits are confirmed, bookings move from KYC to registered agreement, demands follow certified milestones and possession runs from one snag list.

What makes residential developers different

  • Launch weekends bring a flood of portal, ad and hoarding enquiries that pre-sales cannot call back fast enough, and attribution between sources and partners is unreliable.

  • Site visits are booked by phone, buyers forget or arrive at the wrong gallery, and what happened during the visit never reaches the CRM.

  • Demand letters are prepared in spreadsheets from the ERP, checked by hand and sent without the progress evidence that buyers and their lenders ask for.

  • Possession brings a rush of handover appointments, final dues queries and snag complaints tracked on calls and paper.

Where automation helps residential developers

  • Fast, consented lead response

    Portal, Meta, Google, website and missed-call leads deduplicated and answered in minutes with the brochure and RERA registration number, then qualified and assigned with response-time alerts.

  • Site visits that actually happen

    WhatsApp visit booking against gallery capacity, reminders with the location pin, QR check-in that confirms partner attribution, and visit notes summarized into the CRM.

  • NRI desk across time zones

    Replies and updates in the buyer's own daytime, video site visits, and answers on eligibility and NRE, NRO or FCNR payments drawn only from an FAQ your legal team approves.

  • Booking desk on one record

    Secure KYC links, allotment letters and agreement drafts from legal-approved templates, registration appointments, a control on advances before the registered agreement, and home-loan cases tracked by lender.

  • Milestone demands with evidence

    Demand letters released only after the architect's or engineer's certificate and finance approval, sent with photos of the completed stage and disbursement request packs for lenders.

  • Possession and snag control

    Handover slots, final dues statements, room-by-room snag reporting with photos, contractor assignment with verified closure, and defect tickets that stay open after handover.

Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Portal and ad lead capture with fast response and qualification

Enquiries from property portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website and missed-call numbers reach one CRM queue within minutes, are deduplicated and answered with approved project content, then qualified and assigned to an executive with response-time alerts.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Portal and ad leads arrive at all hours into separate dashboards and inboxes. The same buyer enquires on several portals, nobody owns the first call, and slow follow-up wastes media spend. Generic chatbots, meanwhile, risk quoting the wrong price or promising a possession date.

Trigger

A lead arrives from a portal such as 99acres, MagicBricks or Housing.com through the API or export its package offers, a Meta or Google lead form, the website, a missed-call number or a QR code on a hoarding.

How it runs

  1. Normalize the phone number and project, match the lead against CRM records by phone, email and portal lead ID, and merge duplicates while keeping every source for attribution.
  2. Read the consent captured by the source form: opted-in leads get an approved WhatsApp template with the brochure, RERA registration number and next steps; others get a call through the registered telephony set-up, and the executive offers the opt-in.
  3. Collect configuration, budget band, preferred location, purchase timeline, home-loan need and resident or NRI status through a short WhatsApp Flow or the executive's call script.
  4. Answer questions on amenities, location, carpet area and price range only from the approved project knowledge base, citing the entry used; offers, discounts and possession dates are handed to the executive.
  5. Score the lead against rules the sales head sets, assign it by project, language or round robin, and alert the sales manager when no meaningful contact happens within the agreed window.
  6. Report response time, qualification and cost per qualified lead by source, campaign and portal package every week.

Human checkpoint

The assigned executive owns every qualified conversation and makes the first call where there is no WhatsApp opt-in. Prices come only from the approved price sheet; offers, discounts, payment-plan changes and possession dates go to the executive or sales manager. Marketing and legal approve all templates.

Visit and evaluateStandard3–4 weeks

Site visit booking, reminders, check-in and post-visit follow-up

Qualified buyers book a site visit on WhatsApp against sales gallery capacity, receive reminders with the location pin, check in by QR code on arrival and get a feedback request afterwards, while the executive's notes become a confirmed CRM summary and next step.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Visits are booked over the phone and forgotten, buyers arrive at the wrong gallery or at the busiest hour, and what happened during the visit lives in the executive's head. Interested buyers cool off because nobody follows up with the right unit, floor plan or cost sheet at the right time.

Trigger

A qualified lead accepts a visit in the WhatsApp Flow, an executive books one in the CRM, or a channel partner books one for a registered client.

How it runs

  1. Offer visit slots by project and gallery based on executive rosters and weekend capacity, and write the booking to the CRM against the lead and any partner registration.
  2. Confirm with an approved template carrying the location pin, parking and what to bring, then send reminders the day before and a few hours before with reschedule and cancel buttons.
  3. On arrival, a QR check-in at the gallery records the visit, alerts the assigned executive and confirms attribution for any registered partner.
  4. After the visit, the executive dictates or types notes; AI drafts a summary of units shown, objections and next step, which the executive confirms before it is saved.
  5. Send a short feedback request and the follow-up content the executive selected, such as the floor plan or cost sheet, and schedule the agreed callback.
  6. Show no-shows, revisits and visit-to-booking conversion by project, source, partner and executive.

Human checkpoint

Executives confirm every AI visit summary before it enters the CRM and choose what follow-up content is sent. Cost sheets are generated only from the approved price sheet, and the sales manager reviews hot leads and any negotiation every day.

Visit and evaluateStandard3–5 weeks

NRI buyer nurturing across time zones with video site visits

Buyers abroad get replies and updates in their own daytime, book video site visits that overlap with Indian working hours, and receive answers on eligibility, payments and documentation only from content your legal team approves, with an NRI desk manager owning every relationship.

Residential developers · Brokers & channel partners

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

NRI enquiries arrive overnight Indian time and wait until morning, and follow-ups land in the middle of the buyer's night. Questions about NRE or NRO payments, power of attorney and repatriation get informal, inconsistent answers from different executives, and family members in India are left out of the conversation.

Trigger

A lead is identified as living abroad by its country code, a form answer or the executive's tag in the CRM.

How it runs

  1. Record the buyer's country, time zone and preferred contact hours, and collect a WhatsApp and email opt-in that names the developer.
  2. Schedule replies, reminders and updates inside the buyer's local daytime, with a live handover to the NRI desk during overlapping hours.
  3. Offer a video site visit with an executive at the project, and invite a family member the buyer nominates in India to a physical visit if the buyer wishes.
  4. Answer questions on eligibility, payment through NRE, NRO or FCNR accounts or inward remittance, power of attorney and documents only from the FAQ legal approves; tax and individual cases go to the legal team or the buyer's adviser.
  5. Send a monthly email digest of construction progress and new releases to opted-in buyers, with an unsubscribe link in every email.
  6. Track responses, video visits and bookings by country and source.

Human checkpoint

The NRI desk relationship manager owns each buyer and handles every pricing, booking and documentation conversation. Legal approves the FAQ and the power of attorney guidance, and no automated message gives tax or foreign exchange advice on an individual case.

Book, document and financeAdvanced6–8 weeks

Booking to registered agreement: KYC, allotment and home loans

After a booking, buyers complete a secure application with KYC, the CRM team verifies it, allotment letters and agreement drafts come from legal-approved templates, demands stay within the RERA advance limit until registration, and each home-loan case is tracked with the buyer's lender.

Residential developers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Booking forms, KYC copies, payment proofs, allotment letters and agreement drafts move between sales, CRM, legal, finance and lenders by email and paper. Missing documents delay registration, demands can exceed the advance RERA allows before a registered agreement, and buyers cannot tell where their loan or paperwork stands.

Trigger

A sales executive marks a unit as booked in the CRM or ERP and the booking amount is received through the bank or payment gateway.

How it runs

  1. Send the buyer a secure, expiring link to complete the application for every applicant, upload PAN and address proof, or passport and overseas address proof, or the OCI card, for NRI and OCI buyers, and confirm the unit, price and payment plan.
  2. Match the booking amount against bank or gateway records, and block any further demand above the advance RERA permits until the agreement for sale is registered.
  3. Queue the file for CRM verification; once verified, generate the allotment letter from the legal-approved template and send it for authorized signature.
  4. If the buyer needs a loan, record their consent to share status with the lender they choose, send that lender's checklist and the list of banks that have approved the project, and track sanction and any tripartite agreement.
  5. Prepare the agreement for sale from the state's prescribed format for legal review, book the registration appointment, and track stamp duty and registration fees.
  6. Keep the buyer informed at each step with approved WhatsApp and email updates, and show every file's status and blocker on a CRM team board.

Human checkpoint

The CRM team verifies every KYC file and legal approves every allotment letter and agreement. Any deviation in price, payment plan or terms needs the sales head and finance controller. Lenders decide loans, and nothing is shared with a lender without the buyer's consent.

Build and payAdvanced5–7 weeks

Construction progress updates and milestone-linked demand letters

When the project's architect or engineer certifies a construction stage, buyers receive a progress update with photos and a demand letter calculated from their payment plan, once finance approves the batch. Lenders get disbursement requests for loan buyers, and monthly updates fill the gaps.

Residential developers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Demand letters are compiled from the ERP in spreadsheets, checked by hand and sent without evidence that the stage is complete. Buyers and lenders push back, disbursements arrive late and collections slip. Progress updates are irregular and sometimes disagree with what the developer files on the RERA portal.

Trigger

A construction stage in the payment plan, such as a slab or masonry milestone, is certified by the project's architect or engineer and approved by the project head in the ERP, or the monthly update date arrives.

How it runs

  1. Collect the stage certificate, site photos and tower-wise progress from the site team's reports, and draft a plain-language update from those facts only.
  2. Route the update to the project head and marketing for approval, checking stated progress against the figures in the latest RERA quarterly update.
  3. Generate demand letters per unit from the payment plan with amount, taxes, due date and the project's designated collection account, and run a maker-checker review of totals and a sample of letters.
  4. Release the approved batch by email with the letter and update, plus a WhatsApp notification with a secure link to opted-in buyers, and send lenders disbursement request packs for loan buyers who consented to lender sharing.
  5. Remind buyers before the due date, match receipts from bank statements, and pass overdue cases to the CRM team with history; any interest under the agreement is calculated for finance to review, never applied automatically.
  6. Show demanded, collected and overdue amounts by tower and milestone, and disbursement requests pending with each lender.

Human checkpoint

No demand goes out without the architect's or engineer's certificate, the project head's approval and the finance controller's batch approval. Interest, waivers and payment-plan changes are decided by finance and the CRM head, and the project head approves every progress statement.

Possession and move-inStandard4–6 weeks

Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list management

After the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion, buyers and tenants book handover slots, receive a final dues statement, report snags room by room with photos and track each item as the contractor fixes it and a quality engineer verifies it. Later defect reports follow the same path.

Residential developers · Commercial leasing & co-working · Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Possession arrives in a rush: buyers call for dates and final dues, snag lists are written on paper during the walkthrough, and contractors receive them days later on WhatsApp. Items are closed without proof and reopened by unhappy buyers, and defect complaints after handover get lost although the developer remains responsible for years.

Trigger

The occupancy certificate is received and possession is offered for a tower, or a commercial floor's warm-shell or fit-out handover is ready; later, an owner or tenant reports a defect.

How it runs

  1. Send the possession or handover offer with the final dues statement and document checklist, and offer handover slots by tower and floor.
  2. During the pre-handover inspection, buyers or tenants log snags room by room with photos and a category, on a tablet with the handover executive or on their own phone.
  3. Assign each snag to the responsible contractor or trade with a due date, and notify the contractor's site engineer.
  4. Contractors close items with after photos, and the quality engineer verifies each closure before the buyer or tenant is asked to confirm.
  5. Release keys or access once dues, documents and the agreed snags are complete, and record the handover acknowledgement.
  6. Keep a defect reporting route open after handover, tracked as defect-liability tickets with the same assignment and verification steps.

Human checkpoint

The quality engineer verifies every closure and the CRM handover manager signs off each possession. Disputed snags, compensation questions and any structural concern go to the project head and, where needed, the structural consultant.

Handover and defect records are kept for at least the defect liability period, which RERA sets at five years from possession for units sold in registered projects.

  • Snag reopen rate
  • Defect tickets open beyond target
  • Handover satisfaction score
